## Overview

This companion to [LRP76](../lrp-rli-med-076) swaps mediator and outcome: word reading at t2 predicts letter-sound knowledge at t4 under an assumed reverse direction. The lagged DAG includes $WR_t \rightarrow LS_{t+1}$ for this hypothesis. Roch and Jarrold (2012, DOI [10.1016/j.jcomdis.2011.11.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcomdis.2011.11.001)) reported word reading as a longitudinal predictor of later nonword reading; this does not identify an effect on letter-sound knowledge. See the [design record](../../../notes/202607172100-reverse-mediation-wr-ls-direction-spec.md) for the rationale and interpretation corrections.

## Design

Mediator $W_{t2}$ (Beta-Binomial on $W_{t1}$); outcome $L_{t4}$ (conditioned on $L_{t1}$, loaded via the lagged-outcome preparation). Adjustment $\{G, A, W_\text{pre}, W_{t1}, HS, SP\}$ — the exogenous common causes of the mediator $WR$ and the outcome $LS$ (hearing `hs`, speech `deapp_c`) at baseline. Phonological memory $RW$ and baseline vocabulary $E/R$ are **not** $WR \leftrightarrow LS$ confounders (they cause $WR$ but not $LS$), so they are omitted — the asymmetry vs LRP76. The t3-outcome ceiling-sensitivity companion is [LRP276](../lrp-rli-med-276).

## Assumptions — read this first {#sec-assumptions}

Assignment still randomises treatment schedules after crossover. Word reading is not randomised as a mediator, and latent ability and treatment-induced dose can confound its association with later letter-sound knowledge. This decomposition assumes a reverse direction; it does not establish that direction. The intervention can affect several skills, so assignment is not an isolated experimental change in either word reading or letter sounds. Check ceiling support and compare with the t3-outcome companion without treating that comparison as an isolated ceiling correction.
